clue.text: On which nothing is calm

parts.note: reads like a remark about a restless place, but describes a wind-force table whose zero reading is labelled calm

explanation.surface: A gloomy observation about some place where there is never any peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing' is the number zero: on the wind-force table devised by Admiral Beaufort, force 0 is called 'calm'.
explanation.definitionFit: The wind-force table runs from 0, described as calm, up to 12, hurricane.

clue.text: Essentially wheeled out deranged spirit

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Essentially wheeled out deranged spirit (9)': MENTAL (deranged) gives the end and 'spirit' the definition, but no reading of 'Essentially wheeled out' gives ELE; the clue looks garbled and no other print was found

clue.text: Found ideas not fully ruined?

indicators.note: the two words are not used in full, so only a run of letters from inside them counts

explanation.surface: Someone's discovered theories have perhaps been wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the F from 'Found' and the EAS from 'ideas': fo(UND IDe)as.
explanation.definitionFit: To have undone someone is to have brought about their ruin, so the past tense matches 'ruined'.

clue.text: More than one Isle of Skye? No, right out

indicators.note: out in the sense of disordered or wrong, telling us to rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Skye is one of several islands and is told flatly no.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of SKYE + NO + R gives the plural name of the Scottish island group north of the mainland; Skye itself belongs to the Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orkney Islands are an archipelago off northern Scotland, so the plural form names more than one isle.

clue.text: Risk sea god devouring you initially?

indicators.note: the sea god swallows something, so another piece goes inside his name

parts.note: Triton is the Greek merman god of the sea, son of Poseidon

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word 'you' is taken

explanation.surface: A question about whether it is dangerous for a sea deity to eat you.
explanation.walkthrough: The Y from 'you initially' goes inside TRITON, after TR.
explanation.definitionFit: To attempt something cheeky to see what one can get away with is taking a chance, a gamble.

clue.text: Unchaste wife teased one served at the bar?

indicators.note: teasing pulls fibres apart and loosens them, so these letters are pulled into a new order

explanation.surface: A promiscuous spouse flirts with a man who is waiting on drinkers in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a barman being served, but what is served at the bar is a snack in a little bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Salted kernels from a tropical tree are a typical pub snack served alongside drinks.

clue.text: Comic famous author left for women

indicators.note: one letter is put in place of another, the first standing for the second

parts.note: Evelyn Waugh, the English novelist of Brideshead Revisited

explanation.surface: A comedian, a well-known novelist, abandoned his wife and went off with other women.
explanation.walkthrough: In WAUGH the W (women) is replaced by L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: Calling a person 'a real laugh' means they are funny company, a joker.

clue.text: A novel stew of chorizo got Monday gravadlax in the middle

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'A novel stew of chorizo got Monday gravadlax in the middle (6,7)': the anagram of CHORIZO GOT plus VAD (middle of gravadlax) gives the answer, leaving 'Monday' with no job; probably a misprint, no other print found
annotationWithheld.clue: A novel stew of chorizo got Monday gravadlax in the middle

clue.text: What might lead you to bed, with hesitation, excitedly?

definitions.text: What might lead you to bed, with hesitation, excitedly?

indicators.note: excitement throws things into a flurry, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A coy question about what might tempt someone into bed, nervously but eagerly.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of BED + HESITATION gives the 13 letters; read as a whole, the clue describes a lover outside a relationship, the 'with' joining the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret lover outside a marriage or relationship is exactly someone who may lure you into bed, nervously and thrillingly.

clue.text: Right round essential party guide

parts.note: O is round in shape
key as an adjective means vital or crucial
a do is an informal word for a party
a key to a map or a puzzle is a guide to it

explanation.surface: A list of the vital things to know when throwing a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal ways of saying all right or OK in agreement.

clue.text: Banger and mash bisque? Almost

indicators.note: to mash something is to crush it into a pulp, so these letters are mixed up
the word is not quite complete, its final letter is lost

explanation.surface: A food question: are sausages and mashed potato nearly as good as a creamy soup?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banger and mash' looks like the British dish of sausages and mashed potato (banger is British slang for sausage). Here 'banger' is the definition and 'mash' scrambles BISQU (bisque without its last letter).
explanation.definitionFit: A small firework that fizzes and explodes with a bang is a squib, so a banger in British slang.

clue.text: Water-plant appearing after short time in river

indicators.note: the plant comes after the abbreviation, giving the order of the two pieces

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
pondweed and other aquatic plants are called weed

explanation.surface: A water-plant shows up briefly in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tweed is a river in the Scottish Borders, forming part of the border with England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed flows through southern Scotland into the North Sea at Berwick, a well-known salmon river.

clue.text: Then trace out a jumper's line

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to follow the outline of a knitted sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' suggests a British sweater, but here it is a ballet dancer, and the 'line' is one of their moves.
explanation.definitionFit: In ballet, a leap in which the dancer crosses the feet repeatedly in the air is a move in a jumping dancer's repertoire.

clue.text: Animal catches despicable types

parts.note: a rat is a rodent, an animal
a hunter bags game, that is catches it

explanation.surface: A creature captures some contemptible people.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratbag is a British and Australian slang word for a nasty or unpleasant person.

clue.text: Helping sort out Laura with two Roman unknowns

indicators.note: to sort out is to rearrange into order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
x and y are the usual unknown quantities in algebra

explanation.surface: Laura is told to deal with two mysterious men from Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Auxiliary staff or verbs give support, assisting the main ones.

clue.text: Figure horse will be found amongst twelve

indicators.note: one piece is found among the letters of another, so it sits inside

parts.note: twelve o'clock midday is noon
a nag is an old or worn-out horse

explanation.surface: A horse is among a group of twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twelve' is the time, midday, not a group of twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: A nine-sided plane shape is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Might you be this, if godlier? Possibly

definitions.text: Might you be this, if godlier? Possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests these letters could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: If you were more saintly, might you be praised and raised up?
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of IF GODLIER gives the answer, and the whole clue is its definition: a more saintly person might be exalted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone more devout might be exalted and praised, raised to heavenly glory.

clue.text: Man reversing sexily almost spirals

parts.note: he is a man, as a pronoun

indicators.note: the next piece is read backwards, from right to left
the word loses its final letter, so not all of it is used

parts.note: taken as written before the cut

explanation.surface: A man backs off seductively, almost in a whirl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts SEXILY to SEXIL, and 'reversing' turns it to LIXES, after HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Helices or spirals are coiled curves like a corkscrew; this plural is a less common form of helices.

clue.text: Long-suffering vocalist losing head in confusion

indicators.note: confusion means disorder, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the word loses its first letter, the head of it

explanation.surface: A singer gets muddled and forgets their lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing head' removes the V from VOCALIST, and 'in confusion' rearranges OCALIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic endures pain and hardship without complaint, patiently enduring.

clue.text: Promise made by a girl eating crumble

indicators.note: one piece eats another, so it goes inside

parts.note: Beth is a girl's name
to rot is to decay and crumble

explanation.surface: A girl tucks into a fruit crumble pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumble' looks like the British baked pudding, but is a verb, to decay.
explanation.definitionFit: To betroth is to pledge someone in marriage, to promise them.

clue.text: Bad horn playing-drum's needed

indicators.note: playing about with something means moving it around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor horn player needs a drum to keep time.
explanation.walkthrough: A bodhran is an Irish frame drum played with a short stick.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish bodhran is a hand-held frame drum covered in goatskin.

clue.text: It says what I mean

parts.note: read as a person speaking frankly, but describes the part of the throat that makes speech sounds

explanation.surface: Someone insists their words are meant exactly as spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a phrase about honesty; literally, the thing that 'says' your words is the vibrating tissue in the larynx.
explanation.definitionFit: The folds in the larynx vibrate to produce the voice, so they utter the speaker's meaning.

clue.text: Search bottom of wide valley

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone searches the floor of a broad valley.
explanation.walkthrough: A combe is a short valley or hollow on a hillside, common in place names in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A combe is a short, steep-sided hollow or dale in English hill country.

clue.text: Poise captured byrunners'jumps

indicators.note: the first piece is captured, held inside the second

parts.note: skis are runners, as on a sledge
P is the symbol for the poise, a unit of viscosity

explanation.surface: Elegance is caught in athletes' leaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poise' means grace in the surface but is the unit of viscosity, symbol P.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip is to hop lightly, so skips are small jumps.

clue.text: Society's desire to be smart

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for society
a wish is a desire

explanation.surface: High society longs to be stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish is informal for fashionable and elegant, as in a stylish restaurant.

clue.text: Grey mammal regularly dropped a girl

indicators.note: every other letter is dropped, so the first, third and fifth letters remain

explanation.surface: A grey animal has regularly let a girl fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemma is a girl's given name, as an example.

clue.text: Authenticated variety of dentifrice, not new

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so the letters are made into a new arrangement
the following letter is excluded, taken out

explanation.surface: A toothpaste brand is declared genuine, though not a new type.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing N from DENTIFRICE leaves DETIFRICE, which 'variety of' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Something certified is officially guaranteed as genuine or verified.

clue.text: A novel one split

explanation.surface: A book about a single person torn in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's novella about a doctor with two selves covers both: the book and a split personality.
